headline: The chief executive of Southeast Asia's biggest bank said investors are now demanding higher returns and closer scrutiny of AI financing, which she called healthy.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: Bloomberg's interview report and a second outlet match the headline; it is a bank chief's view with her own bank's loan total as the only figure.
importance_line: A major lender saying the market wants more from AI deals bears first on investors and bondholders who fund AI projects, then on weaker companies that borrow for them, then on banks; it is one banker's view, and DBS itself arranges AI loans.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by The Edge Malaysia, that Tan Su Shan, chief executive of DBS Group, Southeast Asia's biggest lender, said in a Bloomberg Television interview on Monday 12 Oct that the market is repricing the risks of AI-related investment, with people now "asking for higher returns" and "looking at structures", and that the credit ratings of weaker companies may be cut, a shift she called "healthy" because it checks that big commitments can be repaid. She said DBS has arranged about S$25 billion (Singapore dollars) of AI deals this year, mostly loans for hardware such as chips and data centres, keeping only a fraction on its own books, while Bloomberg notes that interest rates are rising and global bond yields are at their highest in decades.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); read Bloomberg's report on The Edge Malaysia and a second version on Fintech News Singapore; url kept as Bloomberg's own link. Same DBS conference as C05-04, C05-05 and C05-09.
